title: Saga orchestrator: escape hatches and recursion sentinels for multi-tool flows
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: multi-tool chaining (tool->tool->tool), plus streaming responses and structured tool outputs, creates modes of failure we haven't fully guarded: infinite or high-frequency recursion, silent injection of malformed tool results into subsequent calls, and undiagnosed live loops in production. This ticket implements a lightweight saga-oriented orchestrator layer (per-request) that enforces explicit recursion sentinels, escape hatches, and compatibility fallbacks for older SDK clients.
acceptance_criteria: Per-request execution header (X-RD-Exec-Token) is generated and propagated for all tool calls and appears in telemetry events
Orchestrator enforces a configurable recursion depth (default 6) and aborts with structured error payload when exceeded

Streaming tool output that contains structured JSON payloads is validated against declared schema before injection into downstream tools; if validation fails, fallback policy applies (sanitize|skip|abort)
A circuit breaker engages for rapid repeated tool invocation patterns (same tool invoked > N times within M seconds) and emits a stall error with diagnostics
Compatibility shim allows older clients (pre-1.18 SDK) to opt-out of strict schema validation but still receive a warning telemetry event
End-to-end e2e test and benchmark showing <=5% median latency regression for common single-tool calls and documented worst-case behavior for pathological loops
technical_notes: Design: add SagaOrchestrator layer between request router and tool runner. It maintains small immutable execution context (exec_token, depth_counter, provenance array of tool_ids) and exposes three pluggable policies: recursion_guard, injection_sanitizer, circuit_breaker.
Recursion detection: use combination of depth_counter + recent-invocations fingerprinting (sha256 of tool_id+input_signature) with a sliding window TTL to detect cycles that jump between tools.

Streaming integration: validators run on streaming chunks that end with "__JSON_END__" sentinel or final chunk. Early streaming is forwarded to client, but injection into downstream tools is gated until validator confirms schema or sanitization applied.
Injection sanitizers: canonicalize common types (dates, floats), strip HTML, normalize entity IDs. Sanitizers are pluggable by tool interface and configurable by customer via console policies.

Compatibility layer: add request header X-RD-Compat-Version. If absent or <1.18, orchestrator uses permissive mode and records telemetry tag 'compat=legacy'. Customers can opt-in per-route to strict enforcement.
Telemetry: emit events exec.start, tool.call, tool.validation, tool.inject, exec.halt with exec_token and concise provenance. Add histogram buckets for loop-detection latency impact.
Failure semantics: when orchestrator aborts for safety, return structured error with fields: code, reason, exec_token, safe_preview (last validated output), mitigation_suggestion.
Backwards-incompatible risks: strict injection validation may break existing flows that relied on free-form tool outputs. Hence default is conservative; add console toggle for faster rollouts.

Benchmarks: initial local run shows +3% median latency for chained 2-tool flow due to validation; streaming hotpath unaffected when validators pass quickly. Need further perf optimization in C++ validator path.
